articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This article details an SJAA member's experience with a loaned hydrogen-alpha solar telescope, highlighting observations of solar prominences, sunspots, and filaments, and sharing these views with the public at Lick Observatory and a local festival. It also includes a comprehensive calendar of San Jose Astronomical Association events for November and December, featuring general meetings, star parties, and a swap meet.

articles.title: Amateur Telescope Making Class Starting in February
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting an Amateur Telescope Making (ATM) class starting in February, focusing on mirror making and telescope construction, with options for kit discounts and a community mirror. The club also announced its December Holiday Party, a social gathering with a potluck, show-and-tell, and gift lottery. Finally, the article briefly recounted a successful "Summer Under the Sun" solar observing event.

articles.title: 2002 Pocket Calendar Fund Raiser
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is selling "Astronomical Pocket Diaries" (APDs) for 2002 as a fundraiser. These themed pocket calendars, priced at $10 each, include extensive astronomical data and pre-filled SJAA event dates, with proceeds benefiting the club's loaner equipment fund. Availability is expected from the October 6 General Meeting or subsequent Houge Park events.

articles.title: Mooning The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: Akkana Peck and Dave North, regular astronomy columnists, explain their inability to provide their usual detailed sky reports due to their recent marriage on October 7, 2001. Instead, they share personal observations of celestial events, such as a meteor over Moab, Utah, made during their honeymoon. A second contributor confirms this "special conjunction" (their wedding) and provides details about the event, inviting readers to send well wishes.

articles.title: 2001 Fall Swap Meet
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is hosting its first Fall Swap Meet on Sunday, November 4, 2001, at Houge Park in San Jose/Campbell. This new event, following the Spring Auction, is a swap sale for astronomical items, with selling starting at noon. Sellers pay a 10% commission (capped at $50 per item) but no table fees, and Joe Sunseri of Earth and Sky Adventures is expected to participate.

articles.title: Don't Miss The Leonid Storm!
articles.summary: The article announces the highly anticipated Leonid meteor storm, predicted to yield up to 2,806 meteors per hour from three distinct dust trails in November. It details observing plans, including volunteer opportunities for real-time meteor counting projects at Mt. Lemmon, Arizona, and Fremont Peak, California, and provides contact information for participation. Additionally, it promotes a free public lecture by Dr. Lynn Cominsky on "The Extreme Universe of Gamma-ray Astronomy" at Foothill College on November 14th.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: This article recounts a Volunteer Appreciation Night at Lick Observatory on September 15, 2001, where attendees observed numerous celestial objects using the 38.5-inch Nickel Telescope. The author details vivid observations of planetary nebulae, planets, star clusters, and galaxies, often interjecting humor and unique nicknames for the objects. The piece highlights the impressive views afforded by the large instrument and the camaraderie of the observing session.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar November 2001
articles.summary: This document, the 'Celestial Calendar November 2001' by Richard Stanton, provides detailed astronomical data for the month of November 2001. It includes lunar phases, positions and magnitudes for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, along with twilight times, sidereal time, and a highlight for the darkest Saturday night.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This document outlines the current status of the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) loaner telescope program, detailing which scopes are available for immediate loan, which are currently on loan with due dates, and those with extended loan periods. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to borrow an available scope or be placed on a waiting list for scopes currently on loan. The article also lists various types of telescopes, from Dobsonians to spectroscopes, managed by different SJAA members.
